claims.claim: Variant caller achieves 17% sensitivity for variants at 0.001% VAF with 99.1% specificity
claims.evidence: 5/30 variants detected in simulation with single seed=42
claims.falsification_condition: Re-run with different seeds shows sensitivity < 5% at this VAF
issues: n=30 per VAF level is too small for reliable estimate (95% CI: [6%, 35%])
Contrastive learner was trained on full data including test (data leakage in evaluate.py line 104-106)
Only one random seed tested
Performance at 0.01 VAF is 0/30, which is WORSE than at 0.001 VAF (5/30) — physically impossible
claims.fixed_claim: The contrastive learner detected 17% (5/30) of variants at 0.001% VAF in a single simulation run (95% CI: 6-35%); this result requires cross-validation

claims.claim: GNN fusion AUC 0.692, 11.9% relative improvement over best single modality (CTC, AUC 0.619)
claims.evidence: GNN model evaluated on 90-patient test set (420/90/90 split)
claims.falsification_condition: DeLong test p > 0.05 for ΔAUC; different seed produces ΔAUC < 0
issues: Test set of only 90 patients (~45 cancer) gives 95% CI on AUC of approximately [0.58, 0.80]
95% CI on ΔAUC spans approximately [-0.03, +0.18] — the improvement is NOT statistically significant
GNN graph edges are random (np.random.RandomState(42)), not biologically structured as claimed
Single random seed; graph structure may differ with different seeds
claims.fixed_claim: The GNN achieved AUC 0.692 on a 90-patient synthetic test set; this difference from the best single modality (AUC 0.619) requires larger validation to establish statistical significance

claims.evidence: Single run on 3000-patient cohort (1000 cancer, 2000 non-cancer) with seed=42
claims.falsification_condition: Cross-validation with different seeds produces sensitivity < 97% or specificity < 99.5%
issues: NO CROSS-VALIDATION — single seed, single threshold
CET threshold (6.0) was calibrated on the SAME data used for evaluation (run_final.py line 84)
100% sensitivity with n=1000 has 95% CI [0.9963, 1.0000] — but this is reported as perfect
Streak bonus (0.5*n) and trend bonus (3.0*slope) are arbitrary hard-coded values — possible p-hacking
No bootstrap confidence intervals reported
Benign spike model is oversimplified (Gaussian spike with fixed probability)
No CHIP modeling (would affect ~10-15% of screening-age population)
claims.fixed_claim: In a single simulation run, CET detected 100% of cancer cases with 99.95% specificity; cross-validation across multiple random seeds and independent threshold calibration is needed

claims.evidence: Computed as 1.000/0.643 (CET sensitivity / single-timepoint TPR at 1% FPR)
claims.falsification_condition: This claim is ambiguous — what does 1.55× improvement mean?
issues: Compares sensitivities at DIFFERENT operating points: CET at 99.95% spec, single-timepoint at 99% spec
The paper uses '1.55×' to mean both sensitivity improvement AND detection time improvement interchangeably
The ratio depends on the specific CET threshold chosen (which was optimized on test data)
Different CET threshold → different 'improvement' ratio
This is not a validated effect size — it's a ratio of two point estimates from different conditions
claims.fixed_claim: At matched 99% specificity, CET achieved perfect sensitivity in simulation while single-timepoint VAF thresholding achieved 64.3%; the longitudinal design enables detection below single-timepoint noise floors

claims.claim: 5.3× better Stage I sensitivity than Grail Galleri (88% vs 16.7%)
claims.evidence: CET 88% is projected (100% sim → degraded by assumed factors); Grail 16.7% is from CCGA3 clinical study
claims.falsification_condition: Head-to-head comparison on the same patient cohort
issues: 88% is NOT measured — it's 100% simulation sensitivity minus assumed 12% degradation
Degradation factors (-8% sensitivity, -1.5% specificity) are estimated, not empirically derived
Grail was validated on real clinical samples; CET is validated on synthetic data
Different patient populations, different ctDNA fractions, different assay designs
Comparing simulation projections to clinical trial results is not scientifically valid
claims.fixed_claim: DELETE THIS CLAIM or rephrase as: 'Based on simulation, CET could theoretically improve Stage I sensitivity, but this requires prospective clinical validation'

claims.claim: 17-34× improvement in detection earliness (2.9mm³ vs 50-100mm³ tumor volume)
claims.evidence: Extrapolated from exponential growth model and VAF↔tumor_volume mapping
claims.falsification_condition: Empirical measurement of VAF at known tumor volumes
issues: VAF↔tumor_volume model is unvalidated (tumor_volume_to_vaf() in simulation.py)
Model assumes constant 1e-7 effective ctDNA per tumor cell — this varies 100× in literature
Tumor volume itself is a model estimate, not measured
Comparison to '50-100mm³' for single-timepoint is an estimate, not from data
claims.fixed_claim: Under simulation assumptions, CET could detect tumors at smaller volumes than single-timepoint approaches; the absolute volume estimates require empirical validation

claims.evidence: CET detection at day 306, tumor volume computed from growth model
claims.falsification_condition: True VAF at detection (3e-5) is below background VAF (3e-4) in the model — detection relies on trajectory, not signal amplitude
issues: The true VAF at detection is ~0.00003% which is 10× LOWER than the simulated background VAF (0.0003%)
Detection is purely based on trajectory pattern, not any measurement exceeding background
This means ANY rising pattern, even completely within the noise floor, triggers detection
Real-world: noise at 3e-5 VAF is dominated by Poisson sampling (expected ~1 mutant molecule per 10mL)
The claim is mathematically correct under the model but physically questionable
claims.fixed_claim: In simulation, CET detects a rising ctDNA trajectory at approximately day 306, corresponding to an estimated tumor volume of ~3mm³ under the assumed growth model; this represents trajectory-based detection within the Poisson noise floor

claims.evidence: Applied assumed degradation factors (-8% sens, -1.5% spec) to simulated 100% sens, 99.95% spec
issues: Degradation factors are estimated, not measured
No empirical basis for the specific -8% and -1.5% numbers
CHIP alone could reduce specificity by 5-10% in the >60 age group
All real-world ctDNA assays show larger simulation-to-reality gaps than assumed
claims.fixed_claim: Projected real-world performance under stated assumptions is 92% sensitivity at 98.5% specificity; actual clinical performance may differ substantially

claims.claim: Ensemble reduces screening costs by approximately 40%
claims.evidence: 4-tier risk stratification cost model in agent6-ensemble/decision_threshold.py
claims.falsification_condition: Detailed health economics analysis with real cost data
issues: Cost model is simplified — only considers FP workup costs and FN societal costs
Does not account for: confirmatory testing costs, patient anxiety, overdiagnosis, infrastructure setup
No sensitivity analysis on cost parameters
40% reduction is relative to a simplistic 'binary screen/no-screen' comparator
claims.fixed_claim: A 4-tier risk stratification approach may reduce per-cancer-found costs compared to binary screening, with estimated savings of ~40% under simplified cost assumptions

claims.claim: MAML achieves 99%+ balanced accuracy even with 1-shot adaptation to novel cancer types
claims.evidence: MAML in ensemble_core.py uses same data for meta-training and testing
claims.falsification_condition: The MAML implementation does not have separate meta-train and meta-test tasks
issues: MAML trains on all data with no held-out meta-test tasks
The '1-shot' adaptation uses samples from the SAME distribution as meta-training
This is circular — the model is tested on what it already learned
A proper MAML evaluation requires held-out cancer subtypes not seen during meta-training
claims.fixed_claim: DELETE THIS CLAIM or re-evaluate with proper held-out cancer subtypes

claims.claim: 6-18 month lead-time advantage for aggressive malignancies
claims.evidence: Extrapolated from growth model: detection at ~3mm³ vs clinical detection at >10,000mm³
claims.falsification_condition: Prospective study showing actual lead time
issues: Lead-time depends on tumor growth rate, which is highly variable
Clinical detection volume varies enormously by cancer type and location
No data on what fraction of cancers shed detectable ctDNA at 3mm³
Many cancers < 10mm³ may not shed detectable ctDNA at all
claims.fixed_claim: Under idealized growth assumptions, CET-level detection could provide a lead-time advantage of 6-18 months; actual lead times depend on tumor biology, shedding rates, and cancer type

claims.claim: Temporal transformer achieves 100% sensitivity and 100% specificity
claims.evidence: final_results.json confusion matrix: STABLE=0%, RISING=100%, FALLING=100%
claims.falsification_condition: The 100% specificity is on binary classification (RISING vs not-RISING), not clinical cancer detection
issues: STABLE class accuracy is 0% (all healthy patients classified as FALLING)
RISING class accuracy is 100% (all cancer patients correctly identified as rising)
The '100% sensitivity, 100% specificity' claim is for the binary task RISING vs. other, NOT cancer vs. healthy
Cannot distinguish healthy (stable VAF) from benign conditions (transient spikes)
claims.fixed_claim: The temporal transformer achieved perfect classification of rising vs. non-rising trajectories but failed to distinguish stable healthy patterns from benign transient spikes; this model is a trajectory classifier, not a clinical cancer detector

claims.claim: Multi-modal fusion provides additive value over single-modality approaches
claims.evidence: Consistent ΔAUC positive across all ctDNA fractions in TCGA validation
issues: Effect size varies dramatically: +0.010 at 0.001% ctDNA to +0.300 at 1% ctDNA
At the target 0.001% ctDNA, the benefit is near-zero (AUC 0.531 vs 0.522)
Direction is consistently correct across all tests
claims.fixed_claim: Claim is supported; add effect size quantification and note that benefit is minimal at 0.001% ctDNA

claims.claim: Poisson sampling limit makes single-timepoint detection fundamentally impossible below 0.001% VAF
claims.evidence: Expected mutant molecules ~0.3 per 10mL draw at 0.001% VAF with 30,000 GE
claims.falsification_condition: Would require larger blood volumes or higher ctDNA concentrations than standard
issues: Well-established physical principle
Supported by published literature (Avanzini 2020, Bettegowda 2014)
This is the strongest claim in the paper — it's backed by basic statistics
claims.fixed_claim: No change needed; this claim is well-supported

claims.claim: Ensemble sensitivity gain of +6.8 percentage points at ρ=0.3
claims.evidence: Monte Carlo simulation with 100,000 samples and bootstrap CIs
claims.falsification_condition: Correlation structure is wrong (ρ=0.3 is assumed, not measured)
issues: ρ=0.3 is an assumption, not an empirical measurement
Gain depends critically on ρ — at ρ=0.7, ensemble DEGRADES performance
The mathematical framework is sound; it's the parameter that's uncertain
claims.fixed_claim: At assumed detector correlation ρ=0.3, the ensemble provides +6.8pp sensitivity gain; empirical measurement of ρ is needed
